title: Cabled asymmetric wrap
subtitle: A side-to-side aran-weight wrap with an 8-stitch honeycomb cable panel.
excerpt: An asymmetric side-to-side wrap in aran-weight wool with an 8-stitch honeycomb cable panel positioned along the grow edge. Wingspan approximately 160 cm, depth at the deepest point approximately 45 cm. About 400 g of aran yarn. A warm, structured wrap with visible cable architecture.
sourceNotes: The honeycomb cable is documented in Barbara Walker, A Treasury of Knitting Patterns (1968), §Cable Patterns, as the classic 8-stitch alternating C4F/C4B honeycomb. The asymmetric side-to-side shawl construction is a modern application of the cable in shawl form.

glossaryTerms.definition: An 8-stitch cable pattern alternating C4F and C4B crosses on a 4-row cycle. Adjacent crossings create a tessellated honeycomb appearance on the right side of the fabric.

Slip 2 stitches to a cable needle and hold at the back of the work. Knit the next 2 stitches, then knit the 2 stitches from the cable needle. Creates a 4-stitch cable crossing that leans to the right.

content.text: An asymmetric side-to-side wrap in aran-weight wool with an 8-stitch
honeycomb cable
panel along the upper edge. Wingspan approximately 160 cm, depth approximately 45 cm.

The wrap is cast on at one short tip, 4 stitches wide, and grows by one stitch on the upper edge each RS row until cast-off at the other short tip. The honeycomb cable panel occupies the top 8 stitches of the upper edge throughout; as the wrap grows deeper, the panel moves gradually inward relative to the body, creating a diagonal architecture. Budget about 400 g (about 800 m / 875 yards) of aran wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 400 g (800 m / 875 yards) of aran-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 5 mm (UK 6 / US 8) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

18 stitches and 24 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 5 mm needles, blocked. The honeycomb cable panel runs at approximately 8 stitches to 5 cm and 12 rows to 6 cm. If your blocked garter gauge runs 20 stitches per 10 cm, the wingspan at the same row count will be about 144 cm; add 28 more RS rows to bring the wingspan to 160 cm.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 4 stitches. Tail: allow approximately 20 cm. Work 6 plain garter rows. Place a marker after stitch 1. Cast on begins at the narrowest short tip.
Body
RS row (before cable panel is established, sts < 12): k to last 1 st, yo, k1.

Once 12 stitches are on the needle, place cable markers around the last 8 stitches (the upper-edge side). RS row: k to cable marker, SM, work honeycomb cable over 8 sts, SM, k1, yo, k1. (Increase at the new outside selvedge each RS row.)
WS row: k all sts.
Honeycomb cable panel (8 sts): Row 1 (RS): C4F, C4B. Row 2 (WS): k8. Row 3 (RS): C4B, C4F. Row 4 (WS): k8. Repeat rows 1 to 4 throughout.
The
C4B
crosses alternate with C4F crosses to create the honeycomb cell structure. Continue until wingspan reaches approximately 160 cm (approximately 288 RS rows at gauge, giving 4 + 288 = 292 stitches).
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off across all stitches on a WS (plain) cable row. Binding off on a row without active crossings keeps the top edge neat.
Stitch count check-ins
After 80 RS rows: 4 + 80 = 84 stitches. Wingspan approximately 55 cm. The honeycomb should show at least 20 complete cell crossings.
After 200 RS rows: 204 stitches. Wingspan approximately 136 cm. The wrap is approaching full length.
Common faults

Honeycomb cells uneven: the C4F and C4B rows were switched. Row 1 must always be C4F then C4B; row 3 must always be C4B then C4F. Keep a row counter or mark each completed 4-row repeat to avoid switching.

Cable panel pulled in relative to garter body: the cable tension runs tighter than the garter tension. Work the 8 cable stitches slightly more loosely. The honeycomb naturally draws in by about 15% relative to plain garter; this is normal and expected.
Blocking
Wet-block to wingspan 160 cm and depth 45 cm. The honeycomb will not open as much as lace under blocking; pin the garter body to the stated dimensions and let the cable panel settle naturally.
Care
Hand wash in cool water, lay flat to dry. Aran-weight wool can take up to 48 hours to dry thoroughly flat; check centre depth is dry before folding.
What to try next
Add a second cable panel along the lower selvedge, mirrored (C4B then C4F on row 1). It frames the body with a structured ladder-and-honeycomb border around the garter field.
